subject: MAP: POC access runbook and final close timeline
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anne Park <anne.park@lumenly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: POC access runbook and final close timeline

Hi Anne —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our MAP, here is a compact runbook to get the POC environment greenlit so we can hit the agreed close window. Goal: provisioning + connectivity done by 2026-09-10 so your engineers have two weeks of stability testing.

Ask list (action owners in parentheses):
- Org seed: create Lumenly org on Redwood Console and invite SREs (Lumenly) — please share account alias.
- API keys: we will provision a scoped API key for the trial (Redwood / marissa.cole). We recommend ephemeral keys for long-running tests; rotate every 7 days.
- IP allowlist: provide CIDR ranges for your egress and any NAT IPs we should allow (Lumenly eng).
- VPC peering: share VPC ID + account/project details; we’ll send the peering template and SOC/requirements (Redwood / jonas_weber + marissa.cole).
- Data handling: confirm that logs/sample data for the POC can be synthetic or de-identified (Lumenly legal).

Attached: redwood-map-checklist.xlsx (summary + dates).
Proposed timeline (high-level):
- 2026-09-01: MAP & runbook delivered (today)
- 2026-09-03: Lumenly returns org alias, CIDRs, and preferred peering window
- 2026-09-06: Redwood issues API key + peering request submitted
- 2026-09-10: Connectivity validated and smoke tests complete

Can you confirm the owner for org creation and whether Lumenly prefers the ephemeral key pattern? If you want, Marissa can take the lead on the peering template and walk your network team through the steps.

Thanks — we’ll keep this thread as the single source of truth for MAP items and dates.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood-map-checklist.xlsx (11KB)
From: Anne Park <anne.park@lumenly.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@lumenly.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC access runbook and final close timeline

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear summary. We’re aligned on the timeline in principle. Quick answers and a couple of clarifying Qs: 

- Org owner: I’ll create the org alias today (owner: Anne Park) and invite our SRE alias eng@lumenly.com.
- CIDR ranges: we’ll provide our egress NAT CIDR and staging cluster ranges by end of day 9/3.
- VPC peering: our cloud team prefers to review a template first; please send.
- API keys: ephemeral keys are fine for the test. Do you support scoped keys limited to generation-only? We’d like the key limited to generate & chat endpoints, no embedding scope.
- Data handling: legal prefers de-identified examples; we’ll confirm but expect OK.

I’ll loop in our network engineer (cc’d to eng) to ensure the peering window works with our maintenance windows.

One more ask — can you share your SOC2 summary and the minimum TLS cipher requirements we need for the peering? We will need that for our internal change board.

Regards,
Anne
Head of Cloud Ops | Lumenly Therapeutics
anne.park@lumenly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Anne Park <anne.park@lumenly.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC access runbook and final close timeline

Anne / team —

I’ll own the peering template and the API key scope for this POC. Quick notes: 

- API key scoping: yes, we can generate a key scoped only to text.generate and chat.* endpoints. We’ll exclude embedding scopes and disable write-to-storage. I’ll send the exact scope string and a short README for how to call the endpoints from your staging cluster.
- Ephemeral keys: we can issue an ephemeral key pair via our Console API — valid 7 days, auto-rotate. If you prefer longer windows (14 days) we can do that but we recommend 7 for security.
- SOC2 & TLS: attaching a one-page SOC2 summary and our TLS baseline (TLS1.2+; recommend cipher suite ECDHE-based). If their change board needs a full report we can route to security for a redacted bundle (will need an NDA/POC DPA confirmation).
- Peering template: attaching vpc-peering-template.txt — it includes the exact fields we need (VPC ID, account/project, regions, proposed acceptance window).

I’ll aim to submit the peering request on 2026-09-06 if Lumenly returns VPC IDs and preferred windows by 9/3. Also copying Neha on the contact for the SOC2 exchange and any compliance forms.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: vpc-peering-template.txt; redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anne Park <anne.park@lumenly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC access runbook and final close timeline

Anne —

Appreciate the quick responses. Confirming next steps and owners so nothing slips: 

- 2026-09-03 EOD (Lumenly): org alias, CIDRs, VPC ID(s) (owner: Anne / eng@lumenly.com)
- 2026-09-06 (Redwood): Marissa to create scoped ephemeral API key and submit peering request (owner: Marissa)
- 2026-09-10 (Joint): connectivity validation + smoke tests (owner: eng@lumenly.com + Redwood SEs)

I’ve uploaded a signed MAP acknowledgement to the shared drive and attached a one-page DocuSign stub (docusign-map-ack.pdf) to this thread for records. Marissa — please confirm when the peering request is submitted so Anne can book the maintenance window.

If everything above looks good I’ll mark the MAP timeline as active in HubSpot and set the weekly sync cadence (Tuesdays 10am PT) to track progress.

Thanks — ready to run the walkthrough with your network team whenever they’re free.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Forwarded attachment: docusign-map-ack.pdf (3KB)
